description: Diagnose intermittent slowness on requests that Cloudflare fetches from an upper-tier data center through Tiered Cache.
sidebar:

Some requests for the same URL are slow and others are fast. The slow requests miss in the lower-tier data center and fetch through an upper-tier data center, while requests served from the local cache are fast. Tiered Cache activation is per request, which is why the slowness appears intermittent.

## Before you start

Capture the `cf-cache-status` value and the Ray ID for both a slow and a fast request. The Ray ID suffix identifies the data center that served the request (`cf-ray: 3ff26f9cc66f5a4d-EWR`). The slow requests are typically `MISS` or `EXPIRED` in a data center that fetches through an upper tier; the fast requests are `HIT`.

To confirm whether a request was served through Tiered Cache, check the `CacheTieredFill` field in your [http_requests](/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/zone/http_requests/#cachetieredfill) logs.

## The slow requests tier through an upper tier with a congested origin path

Tiered Cache maps each lower-tier data center to upper-tier data centers per your topology. The mapping is static, and it does not use real-time latency between the upper tier and your origin (only [Smart Tiered Cache](/cache/how-to/tiered-cache/#smart-tiered-cache) uses origin-latency data). When the path from the upper tier to your origin is congested, for example because a transit provider on that path is saturated, tiered cache misses take longer without affecting cache hits.

1. Run an MTR from the upper-tier data center to the origin IP, and compare with a data center whose requests are fast.
2. Compare the paths. Different providers or different path latencies between the two data centers and the origin explain the difference.
3. Route the network-path finding to our network team with the MTR evidence: the congested provider path, the origin IP and ASN, and the working comparison. The fix is a network-path change, such as routing that prefix over a different provider.

Do not disable Tiered Cache as the fix for a congested provider path. Disabling it only sends origin fetches from every lower-tier data center over uncoordinated paths; routing around the congestion is what fixes it.

## Tiered Cache activates on requests the origin header-bypasses

An origin response header such as `Cache-Control: no-store` or bare `private` takes effect on the response, after Cloudflare has already fetched the asset through the upper tier. The response status is [`BYPASS`](/cache/concepts/cache-responses/#bypass), but origin traffic still concentrated through the upper tier. To prevent requests from being tiered at all, stop their cache eligibility at request time with a [Cache Rule](/cache/how-to/cache-rules/settings/#bypass-cache) set to **Bypass cache**. Refer to [Tiered Cache and cache eligibility](/cache/how-to/tiered-cache/#tiered-cache-and-cache-eligibility).

## The customer wants a closer or faster upper tier

- **Smart Tiered Cache** selects the upper tier using in-house performance and latency data collected for your origin. It is the topology to recommend when the assigned upper tier is far from the origin.
- **Cloud region hint**: for origins hosted on AWS, GCP, Azure, or Oracle Cloud, set a cloud region hint so Smart Tiered Cache picks upper tiers near the origin region. Refer to [Set a cloud region hint](/cache/how-to/tiered-cache/#set-a-cloud-region-hint).
- **Custom topology**: Enterprise customers can work with their account team for a custom topology.
